_about: Istanbul-Bogazici, 12 Oct 2026 — §8, the four readings. Every stop is one of this guide's own cards or table venues, with the hours those cards carry (re-checked 12 Oct 2026; where listings disagree the card says call, and so does the step).

onenight.title: Une nuit
onenight.kicker: One night ashore · pick the quarter you are berthed nearest · walking order
onenight.lede: Istanbul eats late and drinks slowly: the meyhane table runs from eight for three or four hours, and the soup counters keep the night going after it. Each quarter below is one evening, in the order you walk it. Every name opens its full card; hours were re-checked on 12 October 2026, and where the listings disagree the card says call.
onenight.door_en: Crew ashore for one evening: a plan for each quarter — a glass, the table, the music, and the late plate, in walking order.
onenight.door_note: Le verre · la table · la musique · la soupe

quarters.name: Pera · Tepebaşı and Asmalımescit
quarters.line: A drink above the Golden Horn, the meyhane lane, then the soup that ends it.

steps.name: Mikla Bar
steps.text: The terrace bar on the roof of The Marmara Pera pours without the tasting menu, from 18:00. Come before the light goes.

steps.name: Asmalı Cavit
steps.text: The small family meyhane the city's cooks use after service: cold meze, hamsi, rakı. Evenings only and closed Sunday on most listings; phone the same afternoon.

steps.name: Saray Muhallebicisi
steps.text: Down İstiklal for tavuk göğsü, the milk pudding made with chicken. Daily to 02:00 per Time Out; the house publishes no hours.

steps.name: Lale İşkembecisi
steps.text: Into Tarlabaşı for tripe soup with garlic vinegar against the rakı. The house says it never closes.

quarters.after: Cheaper: the Black Sea pots at [[venue:hayvore|Hayvore]] off İstiklal, which can run out before evening. Spend more: the open fire at [[venue:kontuar|Kontuar]] in the Pera passage (book; days disagree, call).

quarters.name: Galata and Karaköy
quarters.line: The old bank, the jazz club under the tower, and baklava on the way home.

steps.name: Neolokal
steps.text: Maksut Aşkar's rebuilt classics behind the windows of SALT Galata, the old Ottoman Bank. Book; opening days are not published, so confirm when you do.

steps.name: Nardis Jazz Club
steps.text: Up the hill to the foot of the Galata Tower for the first set: weekdays from 21:30, weekends from 22:30 (seen Aug 2026). Book by phone or email.

steps.name: Karaköy Güllüoğlu
steps.ref: card:Karaköy Güllüoğlu and the Güllü split
steps.text: Back down to Kemankeş Caddesi for pistachio baklava by the portion. Listings say 01:00, one guide 23:00: phone before a late walk.

quarters.after: Cheaper: skip the tasting menu and eat the meze at [[venue:asmali-cavit|Asmalı Cavit]], up the hill in Asmalımescit.

quarters.name: Kadıköy and Moda · the Asian shore
quarters.line: A sunset walk, the Anatolian counter, a glass of native grape and the listening bar.

steps.name: Moda and the Kadıköy sea walk
steps.ref: card:Moda and the Kadıköy sea walk
steps.text: From the Kadıköy pier south along the shore to the grass at Moda Burnu, facing the old city at sunset. About 2 km, flat.

steps.name: Çiya Sofrası
steps.text: Back up to the market street and point at the trays: dishes from villages across Anatolia. Walk in; it closes around 22:00, opening times disagree (call).

steps.name: WAYANA Wine Bar & Tapas
steps.text: A flight of rare native grapes on a Moda side street, the list built to pour by the glass. To midnight (seen Aug 2026).

steps.name: Arkaoda
steps.text: Kadife Sokak's anchor since 1999: the garden, then the room. To 02:00 on a July 2026 listing.

quarters.after: The last ferry back: check Şehir Hatları for tonight's last Kadıköy–Karaköy and Kadıköy–Eminönü boats before the second glass.

quarters.name: Balat · up the Golden Horn
quarters.line: A thin quarter at night, said honestly: one great old room, reached by boat.

steps.name: The Golden Horn line
steps.ref: card:The Golden Horn line: Üsküdar to Eyüpsultan
steps.text: The Haliç ferry from Karaköy up the Horn to the Balat pier, with the light going on the water.

steps.name: Agora Meyhanesi
steps.text: The 1890 meyhane a Rum sea captain opened: some sixty mezes, then the rakı sets the pace. Open daily; listings disagree on the close, so book and confirm.

quarters.after: Balat's lanes are a morning walk, not a night one: come back for [[card:Balat: Ahrida and the Jewish quarter|the synagogues]] on a weekday.

quarters.name: Samatya · behind the Marmara walls
quarters.line: Antep kebab on the terrace, then the cure at the soup counter.

steps.name: Develi Samatya
steps.text: The 1912 Gaziantep family's Samatya house: order the fıstıklı kebap, lamb threaded with pistachio. Daily to midnight per the house.

steps.name: Tarihi Mimoza Çorbacısı
steps.text: In Samatya still: kelle paça or the four-soups Mimoza, with a free salad. The pots run until 03:00. Walk in.

quarters.name: Arnavutköy and Bebek · the Bosphorus shore
quarters.line: The best hour on the European shore, then the fire.

steps.name: Arnavutköy to Bebek
steps.text: The yalı fronts standing in the water, then the bay of boats. About an hour; start by mid-afternoon in autumn, when the light goes by six.

steps.name: Tam Ocakbaşı
steps.text: Back along the shore to Arnavutköy, or a short taxi, and a seat at the coals: liver first, then the skewers, a lahmacun to close. Phone ahead, essential on Friday and Saturday.

quarters.name: Rumeli Kavağı · the last quay before the Black Sea
quarters.line: A long evening out of the city, by car, for one fish.

steps.name: The quay at Rumeli Kavağı
steps.text: The northernmost village on the European shore, settled by families from the eastern Black Sea: mussels on the quay and the strait narrowing towards the open sea while the light goes.

steps.name: Balıkçı Kahraman
steps.text: The village grill a two-star chef compares to Elkano: kalkan, Black Sea turbot, grilled slowly. Daily to 23:30 (Sunday 23:00) per listings; call ahead. Ask what came in tonight and what it weighed.

quarters.after: Getting back is the plan: book the car or taxi for the return down the European shore before you sit down.

getaway.title: Le week-end
getaway.door_en: Friday night to Sunday afternoon: the Pera roof, the ferry to Asia, a meyhane night, the bath, and Sinan's mosque.
getaway.door_note: Le toit · le vapur · la meyhane · le hammam
getaway.kicker: The getaway weekend · Friday night to Sunday afternoon
getaway.lede: Istanbul sells itself as Sultanahmet: the domes, the bazaar, a terrace with a view of both. The real weekend is on the water and across it: a commuter ferry to Asia for the price of a bus fare, a market lunch in Kadıköy at a counter that collects village recipes, a four-hour rakı table in the lanes the minorities built, a bath on the clock, and the mosque Sinan built on the third hill. Every stop below is already in this guide and was re-checked on 12 October 2026. This reading puts them in order, and tells you what to book before you fly.
book: [[venue:mikla|Mikla]] — online for Friday dinner; a card guarantee of €35 a head, and the table is released 30 minutes after your slot.
[[venue:asmali-cavit|Asmalı Cavit]] — by phone for Saturday night; it is small and closed on Sunday.
[[card:Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı|Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı]] — online or by phone for Sunday; women 08:00–16:00, men from 16:30. A mixed party books [[card:Ağa Hamamı|Ağa Hamamı]] instead.
[[card:Nardis Jazz Club|Nardis Jazz Club]] — by phone or email for Friday's late set.

days.label: Friday
days.title: The Pera roof and the tower

stops.name: Dinner at Mikla
stops.text: The roof of The Marmara Pera and the kitchen that coined the phrase New Anatolian. Take the six-course tasting and come early for the terrace bar while the light is on the Golden Horn.
stops.meta: The Marmara Pera, Tepebaşı · six-course tasting ₺10,500 (house menu, Aug 2026) · book online · smart chic

stops.name: Nardis Jazz Club
stops.text: Walk down from Tepebaşı to the foot of the Galata Tower, to the city's oldest dedicated jazz club, in a Genoese building.
stops.meta: Galata · weekends 22:30–01:30 (seen Aug 2026) · book by phone or email

stops.name: Baklava at Karaköy Güllüoğlu
stops.ref: card:Karaköy Güllüoğlu and the Güllü split
stops.text: Down the hill to Karaköy for fıstıklı kuru baklava by the portion, the drier, crisper build.
stops.meta: Kemankeş Cad. 67 · to 01:00 per listings, 23:00 per one guide: phone

days.label: Saturday
days.title: Across to Asia, and the meyhane night

stops.name: Serpme breakfast at Van Kahvaltı Evi
stops.text: Cihangir's Van house: the herb cheese first, then the spread. No bookings, and the weekend queue is real, so go early.
stops.meta: Cihangir · daily from breakfast; listings disagree on the times · walk in

stops.name: The vapur from Karaköy to Kadıköy
stops.text: The best room in the city costs a commuter fare: twenty minutes on deck, tea from the tray, Europe behind you and Asia ahead.
stops.meta: Karaköy or Eminönü pier · about 20–25 minutes · an İstanbulkart

stops.name: Kadıköy market
stops.ref: card:Kadıköy market and the Tuesday pazar
stops.text: Five minutes up from the pier: the fish row, the greengrocers, palamut whole on the ice in autumn. Fullest in the late morning.
stops.meta: Güneşlibahçe Sokağı and the streets round it · daily

stops.name: Lunch at Çiya Sofrası
stops.text: Musa Dağdeviren's counter of recipes collected village by village. Point at what you cannot name; the zeytinyağlı trays and the mantı rotate.
stops.meta: Güneşlibahçe Sok. 43 · daily, lunch and dinner · walk in · about $10 a head (50 Best Discovery)

stops.name: Moda and the sea walk
stops.ref: card:Moda and the Kadıköy sea walk
stops.text: South along the shore to Moda's point and the grass facing the old city. In autumn the light goes by six, so this is the late-afternoon hour.
stops.meta: From Kadıköy pier · about 2 km, flat

stops.name: The ferry back at dusk
stops.text: Back across westward with the sun going down behind the domes: the crossing to take in this direction.
stops.meta: Kadıköy or Üsküdar to Karaköy/Eminönü · about 15–25 minutes

stops.name: The rakı table at Asmalı Cavit
stops.text: Cold meze, then hamsi, then whatever the kitchen says; rakı with water and ice, slowly. A meyhane evening is three or four hours, not two.
stops.meta: Asmalı Mescit Cad. 16/D · evenings, closed Sunday · book by phone; opening times disagree

stops.name: Tripe soup at Lale İşkembecisi
stops.text: The Beyoğlu night's last chapter: işkembe with garlic vinegar, in Tarlabaşı.
stops.meta: Tarlabaşı · open 24 hours per the house · walk in

days.label: Sunday
days.title: The bath and the third hill

stops.name: Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı
stops.text: Sinan's bath for the crews of the Ottoman fleet, one dome and the clock on the door: women in the day, men from 16:30. A mixed party goes to Ağa Hamamı in Çukurcuma, mixed throughout. Do not plan anything for the hour after.
stops.meta: Tophane · women 08:00–16:00, men 16:30–23:30 · traditional ritual ₺4,300 (seen Aug 2026) · book

stops.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
stops.text: Sinan's mosque on the third hill, and his own small tomb at the corner of the precinct wall. Time it between prayers; cover shoulders and knees.
stops.meta: Süleymaniye, Fatih · free · closed to visitors around the five daily prayers

stops.name: A glass of boza at Vefa Bozacısı
stops.text: Down the hill to Vefa: thick, faintly sour fermented millet with cinnamon and roasted chickpeas, in the room it has been poured in since 1876. Boza is the cold-season drink; check the counter is pouring.
stops.meta: Vefa Cad. 66 · hours not published by the house

stops.name: Büryan at Siirt Şeref
stops.text: Under the Valens aqueduct, lamb from the pit cubed hot onto flatbread with nothing but salt. The best of the pit is gone by mid-afternoon: this is the last stop, and the right one.
stops.meta: Kadınlar Pazarı, Fatih · lunch; posted hours unverified · walk in

more.title: If you have only one evening
more.text: A drink on the [[card:Mikla Bar|Mikla terrace]] at six, the meyhane table at [[venue:asmali-cavit|Asmalı Cavit]] at eight, and tripe soup at [[venue:lale-iskembecisi|Lale]] after midnight. That is the city in one night.

more.title: The grand night instead
more.text: Swap Friday's roof for [[venue:turk-fatih-tutak|TURK Fatih Tutak]], Istanbul's only two-star, with a Green Star: one long tasting menu, Tuesday to Saturday, booked direct weeks ahead, collar and long trousers for men. Or cross to Kadıköy for the twelve seats at [[venue:araf-istanbul|Araf]], one open fire and a star; midweek is the least impossible night.

more.title: Or the Bosphorus instead of the bath
more.text: Take Sunday up the strait: kaymak at [[venue:emirgan-sutis-emirgan|Emirgan Sütiş]], the shore walk from [[card:Arnavutköy to Bebek|Arnavutköy to Bebek]], and lunch at the coals at [[venue:tam-ocakbasi|Tam Ocakbaşı]] (phone ahead).

more.title: This October and November
items: Republic Day is Thursday 29 October: flags everywhere and ceremonies round Taksim; 10 November stops the city at 09:05.
The Istanbul Marathon is Sunday 1 November: the bridge and the shore roads close for the morning; move any transfer to the afternoon.
The fishing season is open: palamut is in glut, the lüfer run is thin this autumn, and the first hamsi have arrived. Ask at the [[card:Kadıköy market and the Tuesday pazar|Kadıköy fish row]].
The light goes early: sunset is about 18:23 in mid-October and 17:45 by mid-November, and Turkey does not change its clocks.
Lodos and poyraz can cancel ferries in autumn: check Şehir Hatları the same morning before an island or strait day.

more.title: Where to sleep
more.text: This guide does not judge hotels. The weekend is built to be walked from Pera, Galata or Karaköy, where the Friday and Saturday nights end; the only hotels in it are rooms we send you to for a drink, like the [[card:Pera Palace: Orient Bar & Kubbeli Saloon|Pera Palace]], whose rooms we have not judged.

more.title: What we would leave out
more.text: Dinner in Sultanahmet: the monuments are there, the cooking is not. The painted fish-bread boats at Eminönü. Any door with a man outside inviting you in. And the hour before sunset in Ramadan, when the old-city rooms fill in a single minute.
